verses.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ because God wanted it, and Sosthenes our brother.

To the church of God at Corinth. To those who are sanctified (made holy) in Christ Jesus, called to be saints (holy people). And to all in every place who call on the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both their Lord and ours:
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace.
I always thank my God for you, because of the grace of God that is given to you by Jesus Christ.
In everything you are made rich by Christ, in all your speaking and in all your knowledge.
The testimony (witness) of Christ was confirmed (proven true) in you.
So you are not lacking in any gift, as you wait for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Christ will also confirm (make strong) you to the end. Then you will be blameless (without blame) in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful. God called you into the fellowship (sharing) of His Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

Now I beg you, brothers and sisters, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: all of you speak the same thing. Let there be no divisions among you. Be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
My brothers and sisters, people from the house of Chloe told me about you. They told me there are contentions (fighting) among you.
This is what I mean. One of you says: I follow Paul. Another says: I follow Apollos. Another says: I follow Peter. Another says: I follow Christ.
Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified (put to death on a cross) for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
So that no one can say that I baptized in my own name.
I also baptized the household of Stephanas. Besides them, I do not know if I baptized anyone else.
For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel (good news). I do not preach with wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ will not lose its power.
For the preaching of the cross is foolishness to those who perish. But to us who are saved, it is the power of God.
For the Scripture says: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise. I will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent (clever).
Where is the wise person? Where is the scribe (teacher of the law)? Where is the debater of this world? Has God not made the wisdom of this world foolish?
In the wisdom of God, the world did not know God by its own wisdom. So it pleased God to save those who believe, by the foolishness of preaching.
The Jews ask for a sign, and the Greeks look for wisdom.
But we preach Christ crucified (put to death on a cross). To the Jews this is a stumbling block. To the Greeks it is foolishness.
But to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For the foolishness of God is wiser than people, and the weakness of God is stronger than people.
Look at your calling, brothers and sisters. Not many of you were wise by human standards. Not many were mighty. Not many were noble.
But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to confound (shame) the wise. God has chosen the weak things of the world to confound (shame) the mighty.
God has chosen the base (lowly) things of the world, and the things that are despised (looked down on). God has even chosen things that are nothing, to bring to nothing the things that are.
God did this so that no one should glory (brag) in His presence.
Because of God you are in Christ Jesus. God has made Christ to be our wisdom, righteousness (being right with God), sanctification (being made holy), and redemption (being bought back and set free).
So, as the Scripture says: Whoever glories (brags), let them glory (brag) in the Lord.

verses.text: And I, brothers and sisters, when I came to you, did not come with excellency (fancy) of speech or of wisdom. I came telling you the testimony (witness) of God.
For I decided not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified (put to death on a cross).
I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.
My speech and my preaching were not with enticing (persuasive) words of man's wisdom. They were in demonstration (proof) of the Spirit and of power.
This was so that your faith would not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
Yet we speak wisdom among those who are perfect (fully grown). But it is not the wisdom of this world, or of the princes (rulers) of this world, who come to nothing.
We speak the wisdom of God in a mystery (secret), the hidden wisdom. God ordained (planned) it before the world began, for our glory.
None of the princes (rulers) of this world knew this wisdom. If they had known it, they would not have crucified (put to death on a cross) the Lord of glory.
But as the Scripture says: Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and it has not entered into the heart of man, the things God has prepared for those who love Him.
But God has revealed (shown) these things to us by His Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.
What man knows the things of a man, except the spirit of man that is in him? In the same way, no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.
Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God. This is so that we can know the things God has freely given to us.
We also speak these things, not in the words that man's wisdom teaches, but in the words the Holy Spirit teaches. We compare spiritual things with spiritual things.

But the natural man (a person without God's Spirit) does not receive the things of the Spirit of God. These things are foolishness to the natural man. The natural man cannot know them, because they are spiritually discerned (understood only through the Spirit).
But the one who is spiritual judges all things. Yet no one judges the spiritual person.
For who has known the mind of the Lord, so that he can instruct (teach) the Lord? But we have the mind of Christ.

verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I could not speak to you as to spiritual people. I spoke to you as to carnal (ruled by the sinful self) people, as to babies in Christ.
I fed you with milk, not with meat (solid food). Before, you were not able to take it. And even now you are still not able.

For you are still carnal (ruled by the sinful self). There is envying (jealousy), strife (fighting), and divisions among you. Are you not carnal (ruled by the sinful self), and living like ordinary men?
For one of you says: I follow Paul. Another says: I follow Apollos. Are you not carnal (ruled by the sinful self)?
Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos? Paul and Apollos are only ministers (servants) through whom you believed, as the Lord gave to each one.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase (made it grow).
So the one who plants is not anything, and the one who waters is not anything. God is the One who gives the increase (makes it grow).
The one who plants and the one who waters are one. Each one will receive their own reward, according to their own labor (work).
For we are laborers (workers) together with God. You are God's husbandry (farm field). You are God's building.
By the grace of God given to me, I have laid the foundation, like a wise master builder. Another person builds on it. But let each one be careful how they build on it.
For no one can lay any other foundation than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
Someone may build on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or stubble (dry stalks of grain).

Each person's work will be made manifest (shown clearly). The day will declare (show) it, because it will be revealed (shown) by fire. The fire will try (test) each person's work, to see what kind it is.
If anyone's work that they built on the foundation abides (lasts), they will receive a reward.
If anyone's work is burned, they will suffer loss. But they themselves will be saved, yet as through fire.
Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells (lives) in you?
If anyone defiles (ruins) the temple of God, God will destroy the person who defiles it. For the temple of God is holy, and you are that temple.
Let no one deceive (fool) themselves. If anyone among you seems to be wise in this world, let them become a fool, so that they may be wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For the Scripture says: He takes the wise in their own craftiness (tricks).
And again: The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain (empty).
So let no one glory (brag) in men. For all things are yours,
Whether Paul, or Apollos, or Peter, or the world, or life, or death, or things now, or things to come. All are yours.
And you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.
Let people think of us as ministers (servants) of Christ, and stewards (managers) of the mysteries (secrets) of God.
Also, it is required in stewards (managers) that they be found faithful.
But to me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by man's judgment. Yes, I do not even judge myself.
For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified (shown to be right) by this. The One who judges me is the Lord.

So judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes. The Lord will bring to light the hidden things of darkness. The Lord will make manifest (show clearly) the counsels (plans) of the hearts. Then each person will have praise from God.

Brothers and sisters, I have used myself and Apollos as an example, for your sakes. I did this so you can learn from us not to think of men above what is written. Then none of you will be puffed up (proud) for one person against another.
For who makes you different from another? What do you have that you did not receive? If you did receive it, why do you glory (brag), as if you had not received it?
Now you are full. Now you are rich. You have reigned as kings without us. I truly wish you did reign, so that we also could reign with you.
For I think God has set us apostles last, like men appointed (sentenced) to death. For we are made a spectacle (show) to the world, to angels, and to men.
We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are despised (looked down on).
Even to this very hour we are hungry and thirsty. We are naked (without enough clothes), and we are buffeted (beaten). We have no settled home.
We labor (work hard), working with our own hands. When we are reviled (insulted), we bless. When we are persecuted (attacked for faith), we suffer it (put up with it).
When we are defamed (lied about), we intreat (answer kindly). We are made like the filth (dirt) of the world. We are the offscouring (garbage) of all things to this day.
I do not write these things to shame you. I warn you as my beloved (dear) sons.
For though you have ten thousand instructors (teachers) in Christ, you do not have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus I have begotten you (become your father) through the gospel (good news).
So I beg you, be followers of me.
For this reason I have sent Timothy to you. Timothy is my beloved (dear) son, and faithful in the Lord. Timothy will bring to your memory my ways in Christ, as I teach everywhere in every church.
Now some of you are puffed up (proud), as though I would not come to you.
But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills. Then I will know, not the speech of those who are puffed up (proud), but their power.
For the kingdom of God is not in word, but in power.
What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod (a stick for punishment), or in love and in the spirit of meekness (gentleness)?

verses.text: It is commonly reported that there is fornication (sexual sin) among you. It is such fornication (sexual sin) as is not even named among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). One of you has his father's wife.
And you are puffed up (proud). You have not mourned instead, so that the man who has done this deed would be taken away from among you.
For I truly, as absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged the man who has done this deed, as though I were present.
In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together, and my spirit is with you, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
Deliver (hand over) such a man to Satan for the destruction of the flesh (sinful self). Then the man's spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
Your glorying (bragging) is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven (yeast) spreads through the whole lump of dough?
So purge out (clean out) the old leaven (yeast), so that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened (without yeast). For even Christ our passover (Passover lamb) is sacrificed for us.

So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven (yeast), or with the leaven (yeast) of malice (hate) and wickedness. Let us keep it with the unleavened bread (bread without yeast) of sincerity (with an honest heart) and truth.
I wrote to you in a letter not to keep company with fornicators (people who do sexual sin).

Yet I did not mean that you must stay away altogether from the fornicators (people who do sexual sin) of this world, or the covetous (people who want what belongs to others), or extortioners (cheaters), or idolaters (people who worship idols). For then you would need to go out of the world.

But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone called a brother who is a fornicator (person who does sexual sin), or covetous (wanting what belongs to others), or an idolater (person who worships idols), or a railer (person who insults others), or a drunkard, or an extortioner (cheater). Do not even eat with such a person.
For what do I have to do with judging those who are outside the church? Do you not judge those who are inside the church?
But God judges those who are outside the church. So put away from among yourselves that wicked person.

6.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Does any of you dare, when you have a matter against another believer, to go to court before the unjust, and not before the saints (holy people)?
Do you not know that the saints (holy people) will judge the world? If the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?
Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life?
So if you have cases about the things of this life, set those who are least esteemed (thought of) in the church to judge them.
I say this to your shame. Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you? Is there not one who will be able to judge between his brothers?
But brother goes to court against brother, and that before the unbelievers.
Now there is utterly (completely) a fault among you, because you go to court against one another. Why do you not rather take the wrong? Why do you not rather allow yourselves to be cheated?
No, you do wrong, and you cheat, and you do it to your own brothers.

Do you not know that the unrighteous (people who are not right with God) will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived (fooled). Fornicators (people who do sexual sin), idolaters (people who worship idols), adulterers (people who have sex with someone else's husband or wife), the effeminate (men who give themselves to other men for sex), abusers of themselves with mankind (men who have sex with men),
Thieves, the covetous (people who want what belongs to others), drunkards, revilers (people who insult others), and extortioners (cheaters) will not inherit the kingdom of God.
And some of you were like this. But you are washed. You are sanctified (made holy). You are justified (made right with God) in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God.
All things are lawful (allowed) for me, but all things are not expedient (helpful). All things are lawful (allowed) for me, but I will not be brought under the power of anything.

Meats (foods) are for the belly, and the belly is for meats (foods). But God will destroy both the belly and the meats (foods). Now the body is not for fornication (sexual sin), but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body.
And God has both raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by His own power.

Do you not know that your bodies are the members (parts) of Christ? Should I then take the members (parts) of Christ, and make them the members (parts) of a harlot (prostitute)? God forbid (no, never).
What? Do you not know that whoever is joined to a harlot (prostitute) is one body with her? For He says: The two will be one flesh (body).
But whoever is joined to the Lord is one spirit with the Lord.
Flee (run away from) fornication (sexual sin). Every sin that a person does is outside the body. But whoever commits fornication (sexual sin) sins against their own body.
What? Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own.
For you are bought with a price. So glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's.

7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V36-38 follow the KJV's 'giveth her in marriage' (a father and his unmarried daughter), not the modern text's 'marries'.

verses.text: Now about the things you wrote to me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman.
But to avoid fornication (sexual sin), let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband.
Let the husband give to the wife the kindness that is due to her. And in the same way let the wife give it to the husband.
The wife does not have power over her own body, but the husband does. And in the same way the husband does not have power over his own body, but the wife does.

Do not defraud (hold back from) one another, except with consent (agreement) for a time, so that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan does not tempt you because of your incontinency (lack of self-control).
But I say this by permission, and not as a commandment.
For I wish that all men were even as I myself am. But every man has his own gift from God, one in this way, and another in that way.
So I say to the unmarried and to widows: It is good for them if they stay even as I am.
But if they cannot contain (control) themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn (with desire).
And to the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord: Let not the wife depart from her husband.
But if she does depart, let her stay unmarried, or be reconciled (made peace) with her husband. And let not the husband put away (divorce) his wife.
But to the rest I speak, not the Lord: If any brother has a wife who does not believe, and she is pleased to live with him, let him not put her away (divorce her).
And the woman who has a husband who does not believe, if he is pleased to live with her, let her not leave him.
For the unbelieving husband is sanctified (made holy) by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified (made holy) by the husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean. But now they are holy.
But if the unbeliever departs, let the unbeliever depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage (slavery) in such cases. But God has called us to peace.
For how do you know, O wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, O man, whether you will save your wife?
But as God has given to every person, as the Lord has called every one, so let each one walk (live). And this is what I ordain (order) in all churches.
Was any man called when he was already circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Was any man called while uncircumcised? Let him not be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing. What matters is the keeping of the commandments of God.
Let every person stay in the same calling in which they were called.
Were you called while you were a servant (slave)? Do not let it worry you. But if you can be made free, use it rather.
For whoever is called in the Lord while a servant (slave) is the Lord's freeman. In the same way, whoever is called while free is Christ's servant.
You are bought with a price. Do not be the servants (slaves) of men.
Brothers and sisters, let every person stay with God in the place where they were called.
Now about virgins (people who have never married): I have no commandment from the Lord. Yet I give my judgment, as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be faithful.
So I think this is good because of the present trouble. I say it is good for a person to stay as they are.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be loosed (set free). Are you loosed (free) from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But such people will have trouble in the flesh (in this life). But I want to spare you.
But this I say, brothers and sisters: the time is short. From now on, let those who have wives be as though they had none.
Let those who weep be as though they did not weep. Let those who rejoice be as though they did not rejoice. Let those who buy be as though they did not own anything.
And let those who use this world be as not abusing (misusing) it. For the fashion (way) of this world is passing away.
But I want you to be without carefulness (worry). The unmarried man cares for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord.
But the married man cares for the things of the world, how he may please his wife.

There is a difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares for the things of the Lord, so that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But the married woman cares for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
I say this for your own profit (good). It is not to put a snare (trap) on you. It is for what is comely (fitting), so that you may serve the Lord without distraction.

But if any man thinks he is acting uncomely (not rightly) toward his virgin (his unmarried daughter), if she is past the flower of her age (the best age to marry), and need requires it, let him do what he wants. He does not sin. Let them marry.

But the father who stands stedfast (firm) in his heart, having no necessity (need), and has power over his own will, and has decided in his heart that he will keep his virgin (his unmarried daughter), does well.
So then the father who gives her in marriage does well. But the father who does not give her in marriage does better.
The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband lives. But if her husband is dead, she is at liberty (free) to be married to whom she wants, only in the Lord.
But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my judgment. And I think also that I have the Spirit of God.
Now about things offered to idols: we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up (makes proud), but charity (love) edifies (builds up).
And if any man thinks that he knows anything, he knows nothing yet as he ought to know.
But if any man loves God, that man is known by God.
So about the eating of things offered in sacrifice to idols: we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God but one.
For there are those that are called gods, whether in heaven or on earth. There are many gods and many lords.
But to us there is only one God, the Father. All things are from Him, and we are in Him. And there is one Lord Jesus Christ. All things are by Him, and we are by Him.

But not every person has that knowledge. For some, with conscience of the idol (still thinking of the idol) to this hour, eat it as a thing offered to an idol. And their conscience, being weak, is defiled (made unclean).
But meat (food) does not commend (bring) us to God. For if we eat, we are not the better. And if we do not eat, we are not the worse.
But take heed (be careful) that this liberty (freedom) of yours does not become a stumbling block to those who are weak.
For if any man sees you, who have knowledge, sitting at meat (eating) in the idol's temple, will not the conscience of the weak man be emboldened (pushed) to eat those things offered to idols?
And through your knowledge will the weak brother perish (be destroyed), for whom Christ died?
But when you sin like this against the brothers, and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
So if meat (food) makes my brother offend (fall into sin), I will eat no flesh (meat) while the world stands, so that I do not make my brother offend (fall into sin).

verses.text: Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
If I am not an apostle to others, yet surely I am to you. For you are the seal (proof) of my apostleship in the Lord.
This is my answer to those who examine (question) me:
Do we not have power (the right) to eat and to drink?
Do we not have power (the right) to take along a sister, a wife, as the other apostles do, and as the brothers of the Lord, and Peter?
Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no power (right) to stop working?
Who goes to war at any time at his own cost? Who plants a vineyard, and does not eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock, and does not drink of the milk of the flock?
Do I say these things only as a man? Or does not the law say the same also?
For it is written in the law of Moses: You shall not muzzle (tie shut) the mouth of the ox that treads out the grain. Does God care only for oxen?

Or does God say it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written. The one who plows should plow in hope. And the one who threshes (beats out the grain) in hope should share in what he hoped for.
If we have sown spiritual things for you, is it a great thing if we reap your carnal (earthly) things?

If others share in this power (right) over you, should not we share even more? But we have not used this power (right). We suffer (put up with) all things, so that we do not hinder (block) the gospel (good news) of Christ.
Do you not know that those who serve about holy things live from the things of the temple? And those who wait at the altar share with the altar?
In the same way the Lord has ordained (ordered) that those who preach the gospel (good news) should live from the gospel (good news).

But I have used none of these things. And I have not written these things so that it would be done for me. For it would be better for me to die, than for any man to make my glorying (bragging) void (empty).

For though I preach the gospel (good news), I have nothing to glory (brag) about. For necessity (a duty I must do) is laid on me. Yes, woe (great sorrow) is to me if I do not preach the gospel (good news).
For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward. But if I do it against my will, a dispensation (work) of the gospel (good news) is still given to me.

What is my reward then? Truly this: when I preach the gospel (good news), I may make the gospel (good news) of Christ free of charge. Then I do not abuse (misuse) my power (right) in the gospel (good news).
For though I am free from all men, yet I have made myself a servant to all, so that I might gain (win) more people.
And to the Jews I became like a Jew, so that I might gain (win) the Jews. To those who are under the law, I became like one under the law, so that I might gain (win) those who are under the law.
To those who are without law, I became like one without law, so that I might gain (win) those who are without law. Yet I am not without law to God, but under the law to Christ.
To the weak I became like the weak, so that I might gain (win) the weak. I am made all things to all men, so that I might by all means save some.
And I do this for the sake of the gospel (good news), so that I might share in it with you.
Do you not know that those who run in a race all run, but only one receives the prize? So run, that you may obtain (win) it.

And every man who strives for the mastery (to win) is temperate (self-controlled) in all things. They do it to obtain (win) a corruptible (decaying) crown, but we do it for an incorruptible (never decaying) crown.
So I run like this, not as one who is uncertain. I fight like this, not as one who beats the air.
But I keep my body under control, and bring it into subjection (obedience). Otherwise, when I have preached to others, I myself might be a castaway (rejected).

10.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Also, brothers and sisters, I do not want you to be ignorant (not knowing). All our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea.
And all were baptized to Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
And all ate the same spiritual meat (food).
And all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.
But with many of them God was not well pleased. For they were overthrown (struck down) in the wilderness (desert).
Now these things were examples for us, so that we should not lust after (strongly want) evil things, as they also lusted.
Do not be idolaters (people who worship idols), as some of them were. As the Scripture says: The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
Let us not commit fornication (sexual sin), as some of them did. In one day 23,000 of them fell (died).
Let us not tempt (test) Christ, as some of them also tempted (tested) Him, and were destroyed by serpents (snakes).
Do not murmur (complain), as some of them also murmured (complained), and were destroyed by the destroyer.
Now all these things happened to them as examples. And they are written for our admonition (warning), on whom the ends of the world have come.
So let the one who thinks he stands take heed (be careful) so that he does not fall.

No temptation has taken you except what is common to people. But God is faithful. God will not allow you to be tempted more than you are able. But with the temptation God will also make a way to escape, so that you may be able to bear it.
So, my dearly beloved (dear friends), flee (run away) from idolatry (worshiping idols).
I speak as to wise people. You judge what I say.
The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion (sharing) of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion (sharing) of the body of Christ?
For we, being many, are one bread and one body. For we all share in that one bread.
Look at Israel after the flesh (the people of Israel). Are not those who eat of the sacrifices sharers of the altar?
What do I say then? That the idol is anything, or that what is offered in sacrifice to idols is anything?
But I say that the things which the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God. And I do not want you to have fellowship (sharing) with devils.
You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils. You cannot share in the Lord's table and in the table of devils.
Do we provoke (stir up) the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He is?
All things are lawful (allowed) for me, but all things are not expedient (helpful). All things are lawful (allowed) for me, but all things do not edify (build up).
Let no one seek their own good only, but each one the good of another person.
Whatever is sold in the shambles (meat market), eat it. Ask no question for conscience' sake.
For the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness (everything in it).
If any of those who do not believe invites you to a feast, and you want to go, eat whatever is set before you. Ask no question for conscience' sake.

But if any man says to you: This is offered in sacrifice to idols, do not eat it. Do not eat for the sake of the man who told you, and for conscience' sake. For the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness (everything in it).
I mean conscience, not your own, but the other person's. For why is my liberty (freedom) judged by another man's conscience?
For if I share in the food by grace, why am I spoken evil of for that for which I give thanks?
So whether you eat, or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
Give no offence (do not make anyone fall into sin), not to the Jews, not to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), and not to the church of God.
Even as I please all men in all things. I am not seeking my own profit (good), but the profit (good) of many, so that they may be saved.

11.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Be followers of me, even as I also am of Christ.
Now I praise you, brothers and sisters, that you remember me in all things. You keep the ordinances (teachings), as I delivered (handed) them to you.
But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ. And the head of the woman is the man. And the head of Christ is God.
Every man praying or prophesying (speaking God's message) with his head covered dishonors his head.
But every woman who prays or prophesies (speaks God's message) with her head uncovered dishonors her head. For that is all the same as if her head were shaved.
For if the woman is not covered, let her hair also be shorn (cut off). But if it is a shame for a woman to have her hair shorn (cut off) or shaved, let her be covered.
For a man indeed should not cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God. But the woman is the glory of the man.
For the man is not from the woman, but the woman is from the man.
And the man was not created for the woman, but the woman for the man.
For this reason the woman should have power (a sign of authority) on her head, because of the angels.
But neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in the Lord.
For as the woman is from the man, so also the man is born by the woman. But all things are from God.
Judge for yourselves: is it comely (fitting) for a woman to pray to God uncovered?
Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a shame to him?
But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her. For her hair is given to her for a covering.
But if any man seems to be contentious (wanting to fight), we have no such custom (practice), and neither do the churches of God.
Now in what I tell you next, I do not praise you. For you come together not for the better, but for the worse.
For first of all, when you come together in the church, I hear that there are divisions among you. And I partly believe it.
For there must also be heresies (wrong teachings that divide) among you, so that those who are approved may be made manifest (shown clearly) among you.
So when you come together into one place, this is not to eat the Lord's supper.
For in eating, each one takes his own supper before others. And one is hungry, and another is drunk.

What? Do you not have houses to eat and to drink in? Or do you despise (look down on) the church of God, and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you in this? I do not praise you.
For I have received from the Lord what I also delivered (handed) to you. The Lord Jesus, the same night in which He was betrayed, took bread.
And when He had given thanks, He broke it and said: Take, eat. This is My body, which is broken for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.
In the same way He also took the cup, when He had eaten supper, saying: This cup is the new testament (new agreement) in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you show the Lord's death until He comes.
So whoever eats this bread and drinks this cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
But let a person examine themselves, and then let them eat of that bread and drink of that cup.
For whoever eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks damnation (being condemned) to themselves, not discerning (seeing the meaning of) the Lord's body.
For this reason many among you are weak and sick, and many sleep (have died).
For if we would judge ourselves, we would not be judged.
But when we are judged, we are chastened (corrected) by the Lord, so that we will not be condemned (judged guilty) with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
And if any man is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you do not come together to be condemned (judged guilty). And I will set the rest in order when I come.
Now about spiritual gifts, brothers and sisters, I do not want you to be ignorant (not knowing).
You know that you were Gentiles (people who are not Jews). You were carried away to these idols that cannot speak, just as you were led.
So I want you to understand this. No one speaking by the Spirit of God calls Jesus accursed (cursed). And no one can say that Jesus is the Lord, except by the Holy Spirit.
Now there are diversities (different kinds) of gifts, but the same Spirit.
And there are differences of administrations (kinds of service), but the same Lord.
And there are diversities (different kinds) of operations (works), but it is the same God who works all in all.
But the manifestation (showing) of the Spirit is given to every person for the good of all.
For to one person the word of wisdom is given by the Spirit. To another, the word of knowledge by the same Spirit.
To another, faith by the same Spirit. To another, the gifts of healing by the same Spirit.

To another, the working of miracles. To another, prophecy (speaking God's message). To another, discerning (telling apart) of spirits. To another, different kinds of tongues (languages). To another, the interpretation (explaining) of tongues (languages).
But that one and the same Spirit works all these. The Spirit gives to every person separately, as the Spirit wills.
For the body is one, and has many members (parts). And all the members (parts) of that one body, being many, are one body. So also is Christ.

For by one Spirit we are all baptized into one body, whether we are Jews or Gentiles (people who are not Jews), whether we are bond (slaves) or free. And we have all been made to drink into one Spirit.
For the body is not one member (part), but many.
If the foot says: Because I am not the hand, I am not part of the body. Is it then not part of the body?
And if the ear says: Because I am not the eye, I am not part of the body. Is it then not part of the body?
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole body were hearing, where would the smelling be?
But now God has set each one of the members (parts) in the body, as it has pleased Him.
And if they were all one member (part), where would the body be?
But now they are many members (parts), yet only one body.
And the eye cannot say to the hand: I have no need of you. Nor can the head say to the feet: I have no need of you.
No, much more those members (parts) of the body which seem to be more feeble (weak) are necessary.

And those members (parts) of the body which we think are less honorable, on these we put more abundant (more) honor. And our uncomely (less pretty) parts have more abundant comeliness (more care to look right).
For our comely (pretty) parts have no need. But God has tempered (put) the body together, giving more abundant (more) honor to the part which lacked it.
God did this so that there should be no schism (split) in the body, but that the members (parts) should have the same care for one another.
And if one member (part) suffers, all the members (parts) suffer with it. Or if one member (part) is honored, all the members (parts) rejoice with it.
Now you are the body of Christ, and members (parts) each one.

And God has set some in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments (leaders), and diversities (different kinds) of tongues (languages).
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of miracles?
Do all have the gifts of healing? Do all speak with tongues (languages)? Do all interpret (explain)?
But covet earnestly (strongly want) the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way.

12.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V2 'dumb idols' written as 'idols that cannot speak'.

13.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Though I speak with the tongues (languages) of men and of angels, and have not charity (love), I have become like sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal (an empty noise).

And though I have the gift of prophecy (speaking God's message), and understand all mysteries (secrets) and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could move mountains, and have not charity (love), I am nothing.
And though I give all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity (love), it profits (helps) me nothing.
Charity (love) suffers long (is patient), and is kind. Charity (love) does not envy (feel jealous). Charity (love) does not vaunt itself (brag), and is not puffed up (proud).
Charity (love) does not behave in an unseemly (rude) way. It does not seek its own way. It is not easily provoked (made angry). It thinks no evil.
It does not rejoice in iniquity (sin), but rejoices in the truth.
It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.
Charity (love) never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will fail. Where there are tongues (languages), they will cease (stop). Where there is knowledge, it will vanish away.
For we know in part, and we prophesy (speak God's message) in part.
But when that which is perfect (complete) has come, then that which is in part will be done away.
When I was a child, I spoke as a child. I understood as a child. I thought as a child. But when I became a man, I put away childish things.
For now we see through a glass (mirror), darkly (not clearly). But then we will see face to face. Now I know in part. But then I will know, even as I am known.
And now faith, hope, and charity (love) abide (remain), these three. But the greatest of these is charity (love).

14.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Follow after charity (love), and desire spiritual gifts. But most of all desire that you may prophesy (speak God's message).
For the one who speaks in an unknown tongue (language) does not speak to men, but to God. For no one understands him. Yet in the spirit he speaks mysteries (secrets).
But the one who prophesies (speaks God's message) speaks to men for edification (building up), exhortation (encouragement), and comfort.
The one who speaks in an unknown tongue (language) edifies (builds up) himself. But the one who prophesies (speaks God's message) edifies (builds up) the church.

I wish that you all spoke with tongues (languages), but even more that you prophesied (spoke God's message). For greater is the one who prophesies than the one who speaks with tongues (languages), unless he interprets (explains), so that the church may receive edifying (building up).

Now, brothers and sisters, if I come to you speaking with tongues (languages), how will I profit (help) you? Only if I speak to you by revelation (showing), or by knowledge, or by prophesying (speaking God's message), or by doctrine (teaching).
Even things without life that make sound, like a pipe or a harp, must give a difference in the sounds. Otherwise, how will anyone know what is played?
For if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who will get ready for the battle?
In the same way you also, unless you speak words that are easy to understand, how will anyone know what is said? For you will be speaking into the air.
There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices (languages) in the world, and none of them is without signification (meaning).
So if I do not know the meaning of the voice (language), I will be a barbarian (foreigner) to the one who speaks. And the one who speaks will be a barbarian (foreigner) to me.
So you also, since you are zealous (eager) for spiritual gifts, seek to excel (do well) for the edifying (building up) of the church.
So let the one who speaks in an unknown tongue (language) pray that he may interpret (explain).
For if I pray in an unknown tongue (language), my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful (helps no one).
What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.
Otherwise, when you bless with the spirit, how will the unlearned (person who does not understand) say Amen when you give thanks? For he does not understand what you say.
For you truly give thanks well, but the other person is not edified (built up).
I thank my God that I speak with tongues (languages) more than all of you.
Yet in the church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, so that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue (language).
Brothers and sisters, do not be children in understanding. In malice (hate) be children, but in understanding be grown men.
In the law it is written: With men of other tongues (languages) and other lips I will speak to this people. And yet for all that, they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.

So tongues (languages) are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to those who do not believe. But prophesying (speaking God's message) is not for those who do not believe, but for those who believe.

So if the whole church comes together into one place, and all speak with tongues (languages), and people come in who are unlearned (do not understand) or unbelievers, will they not say that you are mad (crazy)?
But if all prophesy (speak God's message), and someone comes in who does not believe, or who is unlearned (does not understand), he is convinced (shown his sin) by all. He is judged by all.
And so the secrets of his heart are made manifest (shown clearly). And so, falling down on his face, he will worship God, and report that God is truly among you.

How is it then, brothers and sisters? When you come together, every one of you has a psalm, has a doctrine (teaching), has a tongue (language), has a revelation (showing), has an interpretation (explaining). Let all things be done for edifying (building up).
If any man speaks in an unknown tongue (language), let it be by two, or at the most by three, and each in turn. And let one interpret (explain).
But if there is no interpreter (one who explains), let him keep silence in the church. Let him speak to himself, and to God.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge.
If anything is revealed (shown) to another who sits by, let the first one be quiet.
For you may all prophesy (speak God's message) one by one, so that all may learn, and all may be comforted.
And the spirits of the prophets are subject to (under the control of) the prophets.
For God is not the author (maker) of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints (holy people).
Let your women keep silence in the churches. For they are not permitted (allowed) to speak. They are commanded to be under obedience, as the law also says.
And if they want to learn anything, let them ask their husbands at home. For it is a shame for women to speak in the church.
What? Did the word of God come out from you? Or did it come to you only?
If any man thinks he is a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge (admit) that the things I write to you are the commandments of the Lord.
But if any man is ignorant (not knowing), let him be ignorant (not knowing).
So, brothers and sisters, covet (strongly want) to prophesy (speak God's message), and do not forbid speaking with tongues (languages).
Let all things be done decently (properly) and in order.
Also, brothers and sisters, I declare (tell) to you the gospel (good news) which I preached to you. You also received it, and you stand in it.
By it you are also saved, if you keep in memory what I preached to you, unless you have believed in vain (for nothing).
For first of all I delivered (handed) to you what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures.
And that He was buried, and that He rose again the third day according to the Scriptures.
And that He was seen by Peter, then by the twelve.
After that, He was seen by more than 500 brothers at once. Most of them are still alive today, but some have fallen asleep (died).
After that, He was seen by James, then by all the apostles.
And last of all He was seen by me also, as by one born out of due time (born too late).
For I am the least of the apostles. I am not meet (worthy) to be called an apostle, because I persecuted (attacked for faith) the church of God.

But by the grace of God I am what I am. And His grace which was given to me was not in vain (for nothing). I labored (worked) more than all of them. Yet it was not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
Now if Christ is preached, that He rose from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection (rising) of the dead?
But if there is no resurrection (rising) of the dead, then Christ is not risen.
And if Christ is not risen, then our preaching is vain (empty), and your faith is also vain (empty).
Yes, and we are found to be false witnesses of God. For we have testified (told) of God that He raised up Christ. But God did not raise Him up, if the dead do not rise.
For if the dead do not rise, then Christ is not raised.
And if Christ is not raised, your faith is vain (empty). You are still in your sins.
Then those also who have fallen asleep (died) in Christ have perished (been destroyed).
If we have hope in Christ in this life only, we are of all men the most miserable.
But now Christ is risen from the dead, and has become the firstfruits (first part) of those who slept (died).
For since death came by man, the resurrection (rising) of the dead also came by man.
For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ all will be made alive.
But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits (first part), and afterward those who are Christ's at His coming.
Then the end comes, when He has delivered up (handed over) the kingdom to God, even the Father. This is when He has put down all rule and all authority and power.
For He must reign until He has put all enemies under His feet.
The last enemy that will be destroyed is death.
For God has put all things under His feet. But when He says all things are put under Him, it is clear that God is not included, who put all things under Him.
And when all things are subdued (put) under Him, then the Son also Himself will be subject to God who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what will they do who are baptized for the dead, if the dead do not rise at all? Why are they then baptized for the dead?
And why are we in jeopardy (danger) every hour?
I protest (promise) by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
If, after the manner of men, I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantage (good) is it to me, if the dead do not rise? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Do not be deceived (fooled): evil communications (friends) corrupt good manners (ruin good habits).
Awake to righteousness (being right with God), and do not sin. For some do not have the knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
But someone will say: How are the dead raised up? And with what body do they come?
You fool, what you sow is not quickened (made alive) unless it dies.
And what you sow, you do not sow the body that will be. You sow bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other grain.
But God gives it a body as it has pleased Him, and to every seed its own body.
All flesh is not the same flesh. But there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds.
There are also celestial (heavenly) bodies, and terrestrial (earthly) bodies. But the glory of the celestial (heavenly) is one, and the glory of the terrestrial (earthly) is another.
There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars. For one star is different from another star in glory.
So also is the resurrection (rising) of the dead. It is sown in corruption (decay). It is raised in incorruption (without decay).
It is sown in dishonor. It is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness. It is raised in power.
It is sown a natural body. It is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.
And so it is written: The first man Adam was made a living soul. The last Adam was made a quickening (life-giving) spirit.
But the spiritual was not first. The natural was first, and afterward the spiritual.
The first man is of the earth, earthy (made of dirt). The second man is the Lord from heaven.
As the earthy (made of dirt) man is, so are those who are earthy. And as the heavenly Man is, so are those who are heavenly.
And as we have borne (carried) the image of the earthy (made of dirt), we will also bear the image of the heavenly.
Now this I say, brothers and sisters: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God. And corruption (decay) does not inherit incorruption (what never decays).
Look, I show you a mystery (secret). We will not all sleep (die), but we will all be changed,
In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump (trumpet). For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible (never decaying), and we will be changed.
For this corruptible (decaying) body must put on incorruption (never decaying). And this mortal (that will die) body must put on immortality (life that never dies).

So when this corruptible (decaying) body has put on incorruption (never decaying), and this mortal (that will die) body has put on immortality (life that never dies), then the saying that is written will come true: Death is swallowed up in victory.
O death, where is your sting? O grave, where is your victory?
The sting of death is sin, and the strength of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

So, my beloved (dear) brothers and sisters, be stedfast (firm) and unmoveable. Always do much in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor (work) is not in vain (for nothing) in the Lord.

15.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

16.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Now about the collection for God's people: do what I told the churches in Galatia to do.
On Sunday, the first day of the week, put aside some money. Save according to how much money you made that week. Do this so you will not rush to collect money when I arrive.
When I arrive, I will give letters of introduction to the people you approve, and send them to take your gift to Jerusalem.
And if it seems best for me to go too, they will go with me.
I will come to you after I go through Macedonia, for I am going to pass through there.
Maybe I will stay with you for a while, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.
I do not want to see you only in passing. I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord allows.
But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,
A wide door of great opportunity has opened for my work here! At the same time, many enemies actively oppose me.
When Timothy comes, make sure he has nothing to fear while he is with you, because he is doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
So no one should look down on him. Send him on his way in peace, so that he can come back to me. I am expecting him, along with the other brothers.
Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the others. But he did not want to go now; he will go when he has the chance.
Stay alert and watchful! Stand firm in your faith! Be courageous and bold! Be strong in the Lord!
And do every single thing with love.
You know the family of Stephanas. They were the very first believers in the region of Achaia. They dedicated their lives to serving God's people.
Follow the godly leadership of people like them. Respect everyone who works hard alongside them!
I was glad when Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus arrived, because they have made up for your absence.
They have refreshed my spirit, and yours too. So show your appreciation to people like them.
The churches in Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, along with the church that meets in their house.
All the brothers and sisters here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand.
If anyone does not truly love the Lord, God's curse is on them. Our Lord, come quickly!
May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
